body:
## Summary

Feasible, but not on OpenClaw's own spans. OpenClaw runs are already traced: since `f88ee70` (#13), `diagnostics-otel` exports each run to LaunchDarkly as `openclaw.harness.run` > `openclaw.run` > `openclaw.model.call`. What's missing is the link to `openclaw_agent`. In OpenClaw 2026.10.3, no public API lets our plugin put the AI Config evaluation on those spans. The proposal is that the plugin exports its own trace for each run, with a root span that carries the `feature_flag` event, and LLM and tool spans built from OpenClaw's hooks. A new flag turns this on per run. The spike confirmed it with real OpenClaw runs. A root span carrying the `feature_flag` event links the trace to `openclaw_agent`'s Monitoring tab, a few minutes after it appears under Traces. One limit: OpenClaw's public hooks report token usage per run, not per model call.

## Goals

- Each OpenClaw run controlled by `ld-agentcontrol` appears in LaunchDarkly as one trace, with one LLM span per model call and one tool span per tool call. Each LLM span carries `gen_ai.request.model` and `gen_ai.provider.name`. The run's token usage is on its last LLM span (see Feasibility).
- The `openclaw_agent` Monitoring tab lists the traces of runs that complete a model call, next to the Python backend's agents on their own configs. Runs whose model calls all fail are in Traces but not on the Monitoring tab (see Feasibility).
- The trace says which variation served the run (`launchdarkly.variation.key`), so `standard` and `locked-down` runs can be told apart in the Traces view.
- Tracing is controlled per run by a flag, with no restart.

## Non-goals

- Changing the Python backend's tracing. It already links (#13).
- Metrics and logs export from OpenClaw. `run_checks.sh` sets `metrics: false, logs: false` today, and this keeps that.
- Capturing prompt and completion text on spans. Decided: off, matching `diagnostics-otel`'s default.
- Upstream changes to OpenClaw. A public way to annotate the run span would make option B or C unnecessary. Proposing that to OpenClaw is a follow-up, not part of this build.
- Runners other than the embedded one (Codex, Copilot, cloud Agents API). Hook support differs there (`openclaw/README.md`, "Hook support differs between runners").

## Current state

- **Traces are exported, unlinked.** `openclaw/run_checks.sh:51-57` installs `clawhub:@openclaw/diagnostics-otel` into `.state/` and sets `diagnostics.otel` to `traces: true, metrics: false, logs: false`, `serviceName: openclaw-agentcontrol`. `openclaw/env.sh:18-23` sets `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` (default `https://otel.observability.app.launchdarkly.com:4318`) and `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=launchdarkly.project_id=<SDK key>`. For a non-production instance without `LAUNCHDARKLY_OTLP_HTTP_ENDPOINT`, it sets `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true` instead. The commit message of `f88ee70` (2026-10-15) records a local run that exported the harness, run and model-call spans. I read that and didn't rerun it.
- **The link is recorded as missing.** `openclaw/README.md`, "Traces" and the first OpenClaw gap: a probe on 2026-10-13 in `before_agent_run`, `before_model_resolve`, `llm_input` and `agent_end` found no active span. #13's task "OpenClaw: turn on `diagnostics-otel`… Check whether the AI Config evaluation links to its spans" is ticked. The check was done, and the answer was no.
- **The plugin evaluates once per run.** `openclaw/plugin/index.ts:207-247` calls `sdk.ld.variation()` for skill pins, then `sdk.ai.agentConfig()`, and on a disabled result `sdk.ld.variationDetail()`. Then it creates a tracker. `runState` (`index.ts:275`) caches by `runId`, falling back to the session key. `agent_end` (`index.ts:413-431`) sends duration, TTFT, tokens, tool calls and success or error to the tracker. So the config's metrics already arrive; only traces don't.
- **The plugin has no OpenTelemetry dependency.** `openclaw/plugin/package.json` lists `@launchdarkly/ai-server` 0.4.0, `@launchdarkly/node-server-sdk` ^9.14.4 (resolved 9.14.4, with `js-server-sdk-common` 2.24.1), `@launchdarkly/server-sdk-ai` ^2.0.13 (resolved 2.0.13) and `typebox`. `@opentelemetry/api` is in `plugin/package-lock.json` only as a transitive dependency.
- **Versions read:** OpenClaw 2026.10.3 and `@openclaw/diagnostics-otel` 2026.10.3, both installed under `openclaw/`.

## Feasibility

### Can the evaluation attach to OpenClaw's spans? No, not through a public API

- **Verified: no OpenClaw span is ever active.** `diagnostics-otel` doesn't trace the run as it happens. It subscribes to OpenClaw's diagnostic events and builds spans from them with `tracer.startSpan(name, attrs, parentContext)` (`dist/.setup/runtime-api-C7192_s0.mjs:2231-2238`). It never uses `startActiveSpan` or `context.with`. So `trace.getActiveSpan()` inside a plugin hook has nothing to return, which matches the probe. The `@launchdarkly/node-server-sdk-otel` `TracingHook` adds its event "to your active span" (LaunchDarkly OpenTelemetry docs, read 2026-10-30), so it has nowhere to write.
- **Verified: its tracer provider is private.** `diagnostics-otel` builds a `BasicTracerProvider` (`:2661-2666`) and gets its tracer from that object. It doesn't register the provider globally. The plugin's `trace.getTracer()` would get the no-op global, not OpenClaw's provider.
- **Verified: exported IDs aren't the IDs plugins see.** Each hook context has `trace?: DiagnosticTraceContext` and `runId` (`PluginHookAgentContext`, `dist/hook-runner-global-Jvv9WFUW.d.ts:487-492`). That is OpenClaw's own diagnostic trace ID. `diagnostics-otel` sets no `idGenerator`, so exported spans get random IDs. It maps the diagnostic context to the exported one only through a trace propagation bridge, which it registers on `globalThis[Symbol.for("openclaw.diagnosticTracePropagation.state.v1")]` (`dist/diagnostic-events-BADdmgZf.mjs:321-354`). The public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/diagnostic-runtime` exports `formatDiagnosticTraceparent`, but not `formatPropagatedDiagnosticTraceparent`, the function that uses the bridge.
- **Verified: only official exporters get trusted diagnostics.** `createPluginServiceDiagnostics` (`dist/services-D1o7GQlr.mjs`) gives `internalDiagnostics` only to the plugin ids `diagnostics-otel` and `diagnostics-prometheus`, and only when bundled or an official install. Our plugin can't register a bridge or read trusted events.
- **Verified: OpenClaw's spans don't say which run they belong to.** `addRunAttrs` (`:2355-2361`) sets `openclaw.provider`, `openclaw.model`, `openclaw.channel`, `openclaw.trigger` and `openclaw.agent`. It sets no run ID and no `gen_ai.conversation.id`. So OpenClaw runs won't group in the Conversations view today either.
- **Verified: a preloaded-SDK mode exists.** With `OPENCLAW_OTEL_PRELOADED=1` (`:150`, `:159-161`), `diagnostics-otel` skips its own exporter and uses the global tracer. A preloaded SDK with a `SpanProcessor` could then see OpenClaw's spans (option C).

### Can the plugin produce a linked trace itself? Yes, from public hooks

- **Verified: the AI SDK documents the event in its source.** `@launchdarkly/ai-server` 0.4.0 `setLdSpanAttributes` (`dist/index.d.ts:660-684`, `dist/index.js:877-901`) sets `launchdarkly.config.key`, `launchdarkly.variation.key` and `launchdarkly.run.id`. It adds a span event named `feature_flag` with `feature_flag.key`, `feature_flag.provider.name: LaunchDarkly`, `feature_flag.set.id` (the environment ID), `feature_flag.context.id` and `feature_flag.contextKeys`. Its comment calls the event "required for AI Config Monitoring tab trace correlation". It says the Monitoring tab's query is `events.name=feature_flag AND events.attributes.feature_flag.key=<configKey> AND feature_flag.set.id=<environmentId>`.
- **Verified (spike): a plugin-built root span links.** Synthetic traces exported with our own provider, carrying only a `feature_flag` event on the root `invoke_agent` span, appeared on `openclaw_agent`'s Monitoring tab in `jmcgee-policy-agent` / Test (checked in the UI, 2026-10-30). These variants linked:
  - the `setLdSpanAttributes` shape, from the real function and by hand, which has `feature_flag.set.id` but no `feature_flag.result.variationIndex`;
  - the shape LaunchDarkly's own tracing hooks emit (Node `TracingHook` 1.3.39, Python `ldotel`), which has `feature_flag.result.variationIndex`, with or without `feature_flag.result.value`, on the root only or on the root and the `chat` span;
  - the hook shape without `feature_flag.set.id`;
  - with `launchdarkly.project_id` alone, and with `highlight.project_id` alone.

  A trace with neither `set.id` nor `variationIndex` wasn't tested.
- **Verified (spike): the Monitoring tab lags the Traces page.** Traces appeared under Monitor → Traces at once. The first synthetic round wasn't on the Monitoring tab a few minutes after export, but was there on a later check, about 10 minutes after. Between those checks the tab said "No LLM traces detected". See Gaps found.
- **Verified (spike): runs whose model calls all fail don't show on the Monitoring tab.** The four real OpenClaw runs (service `spike-28-openclaw`) were still missing from the tab about 25 minutes after export, well past the lag. They are under Traces. Their `chat` spans had error status and no token usage. The synthetic traces that linked had a successful `chat` span with tokens and otherwise the same root event. Which of those two the tab filters on wasn't isolated. See Gaps found.
- **Verified: the environment ID is available publicly.** `EvaluationSeriesContext` in `js-server-sdk-common` 2.24.1 (`dist/index.d.ts:858-864`) has `environmentId?: string`, and every `Hook.afterEvaluation` receives it. The plugin can register a small hook on its own client to capture it. `ai-server` reads it from the private `_featureStore.getInitMetaData()` instead (`dist/index.js`, `tryGetEnvironmentId`).
- **Verified (spike): `environmentId` is filled in** on the staging instance, in polling and in streaming mode (`node-server-sdk` 9.14.4). Since linking also worked without `set.id`, the environment ID is a nice-to-have, not a requirement.
- **Verified: the hooks carry what LLM and tool spans need** (`hook-runner-global-Jvv9WFUW.d.ts`):
  - `model_call_started` and `model_call_ended`: `durationMs`, `outcome`, `timeToFirstByteMs`, `provider`, `model`, `runId`.
  - `llm_output`: `usage`. The plugin already sums it, with cached prompt tokens counted as input.
  - `after_tool_call`: `toolName`, `durationMs`, `error`, `runId`.
  - The served model is already worked out by `served_model.ts`.
- **Verified (spike): hook order** for a run on the embedded runner starts `before_model_resolve` → `before_prompt_build` → `before_agent_run` → `llm_input`. `before_agent_run` is not first, so the root span starts at whichever hook fires first for a run. That's also where the plugin already evaluates.
- **Verified (spike): `register()` runs 3 times** in one process (same PID). The provider and its exporter must be created once, lazily at module scope, not in `register`.
- **Verified (spike, second run): hook order with tools.** With 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, each tool call's `before_tool_call` → `after_tool_call` comes between one call's `model_call_ended` and the next call's `model_call_started`. The pairs match by `toolCallId`.
- **Verified (spike, second run): usage comes once per run.** `llm_input` and `llm_output` fire once per run, not per model call. `llm_output` comes after the last `model_call_ended` and carries the run's **total** usage: `input`, `output`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`, `reasoningTokens`, `total`, `cost`. `model_call_ended` has no usage. So the plugin can't put accurate per-call tokens on each `chat` span. Only `diagnostics-otel`, which reads trusted diagnostic events, gets per-call usage.
- **Verified (spike, second run): real OpenClaw runs link.** Two successful runs through the probe (2 and 3 model calls, the run's total usage on the last `chat` span) both appeared on `openclaw_agent`'s Monitoring tab.

## Gaps found

### Linking a trace to an AI Config without the observability SDK isn't documented

Filed as #29.

- **What was tried:** finding out which span attributes or events link a trace to an AI Config's Monitoring tab, for spans exported over OTLP without `@launchdarkly/observability-node`.
- **What happened:**
  - [LLM observability](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/home/observability/llm-observability) says to add "the AgentControl config key and evaluated variation as span attributes on the root span", but doesn't name them.
  - [LLM instrumentation](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/features/observability-llm-instrumentation) doesn't cover config linking.
  - The Node.js section of the [OpenTelemetry docs](https://launchdarkly.com/docs/sdk/features/opentelemetry-server-side) says the hook adds span events, without naming the event or its attributes.
  - The event is written down only in a source comment of `@launchdarkly/ai-server` 0.4.0 (`setLdSpanAttributes`). That comment says `feature_flag.set.id` is required, but the spike linked without it.
- **Version and date:** docs read 2026-10-30; `@launchdarkly/ai-server` 0.4.0.
- **Workaround:** use the event LaunchDarkly's tracing hooks emit, or `setLdSpanAttributes`'s. Both linked in the spike.

### The Monitoring tab shows linked traces minutes after the Traces page

Filed as #30.

- **What was tried:** exporting a linked trace and checking `openclaw_agent`'s Monitoring tab.
- **What happened:** the trace showed under Monitor → Traces right away. The Monitoring tab said "No LLM traces detected" for several minutes, then listed it. Seen on the staging instance; the delay wasn't measured more closely than "more than a few minutes, under about 10". No doc mentions a delay, so an empty tab looks like a failed link.
- **Version and date:** 2026-10-30, project `jmcgee-policy-agent`, environment Test.
- **Workaround:** wait about 10 minutes before deciding a trace didn't link.

### Failed runs are left off the Monitoring tab

Filed as #31.

- **What was tried:** four OpenClaw runs exported with the same root `feature_flag` event as traces that linked. Each run's only model call failed (401 from the provider).
- **What happened:** the runs are under Monitor → Traces, but not on `openclaw_agent`'s Monitoring tab, checked about 25 minutes after export. Synthetic traces with a successful `chat` span and token usage linked within about 10 minutes. Not isolated: whether the tab drops traces whose LLM spans have error status, or traces with no token usage.
- **Version and date:** 2026-10-30, project `jmcgee-policy-agent`, environment Test.
- **Workaround:** none for the Monitoring tab. Failed runs still count in the config's error-rate metric (tracker `trackError`), and they can be found under Traces by service name.

## Flags

### `openclaw-agentcontrol-tracing`

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Key | `openclaw-agentcontrol-tracing` |
| Kind | boolean |
| Variations | `true`: the plugin exports a linked trace for the run (root, LLM and tool spans, `feature_flag` event). `false`: the plugin exports nothing; the run isn't traced |
| Starts on in | none. Off in every environment, turned on in `test` for the demo |
| Demo targeting | rule on the `openclaw-agent` context's `agentId`: `helper` gets `true`, everyone else `false`. Only `helper`'s runs (served `locked-down`) then show up on the `openclaw_agent` Monitoring tab. Then roll to 100% |
| Existing or new | new. The plugin evaluates it in the run's first hook, with the same context it uses for `openclaw_agent` |

The three tests:

1. **Observable at runtime:** yes. The flag is evaluated each run, so the next run follows a change, as with `check_live`.
2. **Both states worth showing:** yes. Off is a run with no trace, today's state for a deployment without `diagnostics-otel`. On is the same run linked on the Monitoring tab.
3. **Gates new behavior:** yes. It gates span export, not a refactor.

`diagnostics-otel`'s trace export is turned off in `run_checks.sh` (`traces: false`), so a traced run produces one trace, not two. Decided on review: duplicate LLM spans, with doubled tokens and cost, aren't worth the better before-and-after that keeping it on as the "off" state would give.

An alternative to a new flag is a custom parameter on the `openclaw_agent` variations (for example `trace: true`). That ties tracing to a variation, so it can't be released or rolled back separately. Not recommended.

## Metrics

| Metric | Measures | Derived from | Exists today | Regression looks like | Gets traffic from |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `openclaw-trace-export-failed` | OTLP export batches the plugin's exporter couldn't send | `ld.track()` from the exporter's result callback | build adds | any sustained failures; above 1% of runs | load script, `run_checks.sh` |
| `openclaw_agent` duration | Run time | tracker `trackDuration`, sent in `agent_end` | yes | p95 up more than 10% with tracing on, against off | load script, half on and half off |
| `openclaw_agent` error rate | Runs that end in error | tracker `trackSuccess` / `trackError` | yes | any rise with tracing on | load script, `run_checks.sh` |

## Proposed design

### Options

| Option | How | Pros | Cons |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A. `diagnostics-otel` only (today) | No change | No code; OpenClaw's richest spans | Never linked to `openclaw_agent` |
| B. Companion span through the bridge | Plugin resolves `ctx.trace` through OpenClaw's internal propagation bridge, then exports one `agentcontrol.evaluate` span with the `feature_flag` event as a child of the exported `openclaw.run` | One trace with OpenClaw's spans, now linked | Uses an undocumented `globalThis` symbol that can change in any OpenClaw release; needs two exporters in one process; whether `openclaw.run` is tracked by the time `before_agent_run` runs isn't checked |
| C. Preloaded SDK + `SpanProcessor` | `OPENCLAW_OTEL_PRELOADED=1` and `NODE_OPTIONS=--import ./otel-preload.mjs` register a global provider. A processor adds the `feature_flag` event to `openclaw.run` / `openclaw.harness.run` in `onStart` | Event lands on OpenClaw's own spans | Spans carry `openclaw.agent` but no run ID, so concurrent runs of one agent can't be told apart; a preload for every `openclaw` call; `OPENCLAW_OTEL_PRELOADED` is undocumented |
| **D. Plugin-owned trace** (recommended) | Plugin builds the run's spans from public hooks and exports them with its own provider | Public hooks and public SDK APIs only; root span is ours, so the link follows the documented "root span" rule; we can add `gen_ai.conversation.id` | Duplicates part of `diagnostics-otel`; span timings come from hooks, not the transport; fewer OpenClaw-internal spans (queues, failover) |

Recommendation: D. B and C both depend on OpenClaw internals that the plugin SDK doesn't export. If OpenClaw later exposes a public way to resolve or annotate the run span, B becomes the better design, since it keeps OpenClaw's spans.

### Option D in detail

New module `openclaw/plugin/tracing.ts`, used from `index.ts`.

**Provider.**
- A `BasicTracerProvider` owned by the plugin, never registered globally, so it can't clash with `diagnostics-otel` or with `@launchdarkly/ai-server`'s automatic setup.
- One `BatchSpanProcessor` with `OTLPTraceExporter` (OTLP/HTTP protobuf, `${OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT}/v1/traces`).
- Resource: `service.name=openclaw-agentcontrol`, plus `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` as `env.sh` sets it (`launchdarkly.project_id`).
- `OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true` turns it off, so `env.sh`'s existing guard for non-production instances still applies.
- It's created once, lazily at module scope, because OpenClaw calls `register()` 3 times per process (spike). It's flushed and shut down in `gateway_stop` (`index.ts:466`). For one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs, `agent_end` calls `forceFlush()` before returning.

**Spans for each run.** Parents are set explicitly from the run's state, keyed by `runId`, so no context manager is needed.

| Span | Starts / ends | Attributes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invoke_agent <agentId>` (root, `SpanKind.INTERNAL`) | first hook of the run (`before_model_resolve` on the embedded runner) / `agent_end` | `gen_ai.operation.name=invoke_agent`, `gen_ai.agent.name`, `gen_ai.conversation.id` (OpenClaw session key, decided on review; each `run_checks.sh` check is then its own conversation), `openclaw.run_id`, `launchdarkly.operation.type=gen_ai`, `launchdarkly.config.key`, `launchdarkly.variation.key`, `launchdarkly.run.id`, and the `feature_flag` event (below). Error status when `agent_end` reports failure or the run is blocked |
| `chat <model>` (`SpanKind.CLIENT`) | `model_call_started` / the next `model_call_started`, or `llm_output` for the last call | `gen_ai.operation.name=chat`, `gen_ai.provider.name`, `gen_ai.request.model` (variation's model), `gen_ai.response.model` (from `served_model.ts`), `gen_ai.conversation.id`, TTFT; `error.type` on `outcome: error`. The **last** `chat` span gets the run's total `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` (input plus cache read and write, as the tracker counts them) and `output_tokens` from `llm_output`, plus `openclaw.usage.scope=run`, so nobody reads it as that one call's usage. Earlier `chat` spans carry no usage. Decided on review: per-trace totals matter more than the per-call split |
| `execute_tool <name>` (`SpanKind.INTERNAL`) | `before_tool_call` / `after_tool_call` | `gen_ai.operation.name=execute_tool`, `gen_ai.tool.name`, `gen_ai.tool.call.id`, `gen_ai.conversation.id`; `openclaw.blocked=true` and an ended span when `before_tool_call` blocks the call; `load_skill` adds `openclaw.skill=<key>@<version>` |

No HTTP attributes go on `chat` spans, so they stay classed as LLM spans. No prompt or completion text goes on them either (decided on review).

Each `chat` span's end time comes from its own `model_call_ended`. The span object stays open until the next `model_call_started`, or until `llm_output` for the last call, so the last one can still take the run's usage.

**The `feature_flag` event.** It goes on the root span, with the attributes LaunchDarkly's own tracing hooks send. That shape linked in the spike, and it's the one the backend's hook produces:
- `feature_flag.key=openclaw_agent`
- `feature_flag.provider.name=LaunchDarkly`
- `feature_flag.context.id`: the context's canonical key, as `TracingHook` computes it
- `feature_flag.result.variationIndex`, from `variationDetail()`
- `feature_flag.set.id=<environmentId>` when the SDK provides it

The build writes these lines in the plugin rather than importing `setLdSpanAttributes`, for two reasons. That function reads `__ld` out of handler variables. And importing `@launchdarkly/ai-server`'s main entry runs `dotenv/config`, which reads `.env` from the working directory: from the repo root, that's the production `.env`.

**Environment ID.** A `Hook` with an `afterEvaluation` is added to the plugin's `init()` options (`index.ts:169`). It stores `hookContext.environmentId` when `flagKey === settings.configKey`. It's best-effort: the spike linked without it.

**Flag.** The run's first hook evaluates `openclaw-agentcontrol-tracing` with the run's context and stores the result in the run state. Every other hook checks that value before creating spans. A run the plugin blocks (config disabled or unavailable) still gets a root span when tracing is on, with `openclaw.blocked_reason`. That makes kill-switch runs visible under Traces. They have no `chat` span, so they're not expected on the Monitoring tab, like the failed runs in the spike.

**Dependencies** added to `openclaw/plugin/package.json`, pinned exactly to the versions `diagnostics-otel` 2026.10.3 uses, so one tree is installed:
- `@opentelemetry/api` 1.9.1
- `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base` 2.11.0
- `@opentelemetry/exporter-trace-otlp-proto` 0.222.0
- `@opentelemetry/resources` 2.11.0
- `@opentelemetry/semantic-conventions` 1.43.0

**Setup.**
- `run_checks.sh` sets `diagnostics.otel.traces` to `false` and keeps the plugin installed, so switching back to option A is a config change.
- `setup_config.py setup` creates `openclaw-agentcontrol-tracing`, off, with the `helper` rule in `test`. These are the changes to the shared `openclaw_agent` setup that `CLAUDE.local.md` warns about.
- `env.sh` is unchanged. The spike linked with its `launchdarkly.project_id` resource attribute.

## Risks

- **Failures don't reach the Monitoring tab** (#31). A guarded rollout watching that tab wouldn't see runs that fail. The guardrails use the tracker's error rate and duration instead, which do include failed runs.
- **The link isn't documented** (#29). The event shape is the one LaunchDarkly's own hooks send, so a backend change that breaks it would break the SDKs too. The `tracing` check can't see the Monitoring tab, so the UI check in Phase 2 stays manual. Allow for the tab's delay (#30).
- **Hook timing isn't transport timing.** A `chat` span covers OpenClaw's model-call lifecycle, which may include retries. Durations are compared against `diagnostics-otel`'s `openclaw.model.call` in Phase 0.
- **Runs that never reach `agent_end`.** Spans stay open in the run state. A 10-minute timeout ends and exports them with `openclaw.incomplete=true`, so state doesn't leak in a long-lived Gateway.
- **Two OTel SDK copies in one process** if versions drift from `diagnostics-otel`. The provider isn't global, so the risk is size, not conflicts. Versions are pinned to match.
- **OpenAI cost of the load script.** Each run is a real `gpt-5.4-mini` or `gpt-5.4-nano` call. 50 runs is enough for the duration comparison.

## Open questions

1. **Spike, optional:** with option B, is the exported `openclaw.run` span already tracked when `before_agent_run` runs, so the bridge can resolve `ctx.trace`? Only worth running if option D's spans turn out too thin. Option B would also bring per-call usage, since `diagnostics-otel` has it.

## Tasks

**Phase 0 — Spike (MVP; needs the `spike` label)**

- [x] Export hand-built root spans with the `feature_flag` event to the staging project and check the `openclaw_agent` Monitoring tab, with and without `feature_flag.set.id`.
- [x] Log `environmentId` from an `afterEvaluation` hook in polling and streaming mode.
- [x] Log the hook order for runs with several model calls and tool calls.
- [x] Check that real OpenClaw runs traced this way show on the Monitoring tab.

**Phase 1 — Linked trace (MVP)**

- [x] Add the pinned OpenTelemetry packages to `openclaw/plugin/package.json`.
- [x] Add `openclaw/plugin/tracing.ts`: provider, exporter, run state, root, `chat` and `execute_tool` spans, `feature_flag` event, timeout for unfinished runs.
- [x] Add the `afterEvaluation` hook that captures `environmentId`.
- [x] Wire the hooks in `index.ts`; flush in `agent_end` for one-shot runs and shut down in `gateway_stop`.
- [x] Create `openclaw-agentcontrol-tracing` in `setup_config.py setup` (off; `helper` rule in `test`), and reset it in `setup_config.py reset`.
- [x] Turn off `diagnostics-otel` trace export in `run_checks.sh`.
- [x] Track `openclaw-trace-export-failed` and register it as a LaunchDarkly metric.
- [x] Add a `tracing` check to `run_checks.sh`: with the flag on for `helper`, a `helper` run exports a root span (check the decision log for `trace_exported` with the trace ID) and a `main` run doesn't.

**Phase 2 — Release and demo**

- [x] Add `openclaw/trace_load.sh`: N runs across `main` and `helper`, half with tracing on, for the duration and error-rate guardrails.
- [ ] Set up a guarded rollout (not done: command-line runs share one context key, so roll out by `agentId` rule; see #34) of `openclaw-agentcontrol-tracing` with the three metrics.
- [x] Update `openclaw/README.md` "Traces": the new design, the flag, and why it isn't on OpenClaw's spans. Mark the first OpenClaw gap as worked around.
- [ ] End-to-end check in the LaunchDarkly UI: one run is one trace; `chat` spans show model and tokens; the `openclaw_agent` Monitoring tab lists `helper`'s completed runs only, then all completed runs after rollout (allow for the tab's delay, #30); a blocked run shows under Traces with `openclaw.blocked_reason`; the backend's configs still show their own traces.

**Phase 3 — Optional**

- [ ] Ask OpenClaw for a public way to resolve a hook's `ctx.trace` to the exported span, or to add events to the run span. If it lands, move to option B and drop the duplicated spans.

## Spike log

Probe: a throwaway OpenClaw plugin (`spike-28-probe`) in its own OpenClaw state dir, outside the repo, with OpenClaw 2026.10.3, `@launchdarkly/node-server-sdk` 9.14.4 and the OpenTelemetry versions proposed above. It logs every hook, evaluates `openclaw_agent` read-only with the plugin's context shape, and exports `invoke_agent` + `chat` spans (service `spike-28-openclaw`) to the staging project's OTLP/HTTP endpoint. `openclaw/.state` and the shared `openclaw_agent` config were not touched.

| Time (UTC) | Command or action | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 18:01 | `openclaw agent --local --agent main`, polling, `feature_flag.set.id` attached | Run failed at the model call: the staging env file's `OPENAI_API_KEY` has expired (401 `expired_secret_key`). Hooks still fired, the evaluation served `standard`, `environmentId` was present, and the export of 2 spans returned code 0 (success). Trace `733765bc40dc34fb941e998a5a05e211` |
| 18:03 | Same, two more runs | Same result. Traces `5efbb4ba8b2a682ff7fa8e97bb150943`, `e98340b74fdd15907513b02d6ed77ab1` (both with `set.id`) |
| 18:03 | Same, streaming mode, no `feature_flag.set.id` | `environmentId` present in streaming mode too. Trace `08f7e0195fa27b1b9e9e776f00ab4f7b` (without `set.id`) |
| 18:08 | Synthetic traces (no OpenClaw): root `invoke_agent` with the `ai-server` event shape plus a successful `chat` span with tokens, varying only the project resource attribute (`launchdarkly.project_id`, `highlight.project_id`, both) | All exported and listed under Monitor → Traces in `jmcgee-policy-agent` / Test. Not on `openclaw_agent`'s Monitoring tab at the first check a few minutes later ("No LLM traces detected"). On a later check, about 10 minutes after export, the `launchdarkly.project_id`-only and `highlight.project_id`-only traces were listed. The traces with both attributes weren't reported either way |
| 18:14 | Synthetic traces with the event shape from LaunchDarkly's own tracing hooks (Node `TracingHook` 1.3.39 and Python `ldotel` both add `feature_flag.result.variationIndex`, plus `result.value` with `includeValue`): by hand on root; plus value; plus the event on the `chat` span too; and the real `TracingHook` with an active root span | All exported; the real hook's event keys match the hand-built "plus value" variant. All four on the Monitoring tab |
| 18:16 | Synthetic traces, run from a directory with no `.env` (importing `@launchdarkly/ai-server` runs `dotenv/config`): hook shape without `set.id`; hook shape with only `launchdarkly.project_id`; `@launchdarkly/ai-server` 0.4.0's real `setLdSpanAttributes` | All three on the Monitoring tab. Trace IDs `ee808370b074bd5ea81727f341d1fa8b`, `c208fb6d5cbe93f9f9568ab2e5f6d14a`, `ddd7901c66ae17bdcc3954c4cedbfaaa` |
| 18:33 | Second run, rotated key. Rebuilt probe with the design's changes (root at first hook, `chat` ends at `llm_output` or the next call, tracing-hook event shape, one provider per process). `openclaw agent --local`: `exec` `ls`, then answer | Succeeded: 2 model calls, 1 `exec`, 4 spans exported. Trace `07887345302f1741ddb5d656ed26cc7f` (service `spike-28-openclaw-v2`). On the Monitoring tab |
| 18:34 | Same, two `exec` calls | Succeeded: 3 model calls, 2 `exec`. Trace `41beaff900e16cd07e23668e6f951c22`. On the Monitoring tab |

Hook order for one run (embedded runner): `before_model_resolve` → `before_prompt_build` → `before_agent_run` → `llm_input` → `model_call_started` → `model_call_ended` → `llm_output` → `agent_end`. `before_model_resolve` has no `ctx.trace`; every later hook has one. No hook had an active span. Tool hooks weren't reached in the first run, because the model call failed.

Hook order with tools (second run, 3 model calls, 2 tool calls): `before_model_resolve` → `before_prompt_build` → `before_agent_run` → `llm_input` → (`model_call_started` → `model_call_ended` → `before_tool_call` → `after_tool_call`) × 2 → `model_call_started` → `model_call_ended` → `llm_output` → `agent_end`. `llm_input` and `llm_output` fire once per run, not per model call; `llm_output` carries the run's total usage (`input`, `output`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`, `reasoningTokens`, `total`, `cost`). Tool hooks pair by `toolCallId`.

`register()` ran 3 times in one process (same PID), so anything created in `register` is created 3 times.

Environment check: the spike's runtime `environmentId` and SDK key both match `jmcgee-policy-agent` / Test on the staging instance, and its API and OTLP hosts are staging hosts. No inherited shell variables were set. OpenClaw loads `<cwd>/.env` but never overrides a variable that's already set, and every LaunchDarkly variable was set from `.env.staging-org` first.

Spend:
- first run: 4 OpenClaw runs, all failing at their first model call (no tokens billed);
- second run: 2 OpenClaw runs, 5 successful `gpt-5.4-mini` calls, a few cents;
- 10 synthetic traces and about 14 flag evaluations;
- no Bedrock spend. Nothing was created in staging except the exported spans. They can't be deleted through the API, so they stay under service names starting `spike-28-`; the synthetic ones carry `spike.synthetic=true`. Both probes and their OpenClaw state dirs were deleted.

<details>
<summary>Original idea</summary>

Filed from a Claude Code session; there is no Slack permalink.

> OpenClaw runs controlled by AgentControl aren’t traced today. Send each run to LaunchDarkly observability as a trace with LLM spans, linked to the openclaw_agent AI Config, so the Monitoring tab shows OpenClaw runs alongside the Python backend. #13 suggested OpenClaw’s own diagnostics-otel plugin; confirm that route and whether the AI Config evaluation can attach to OpenClaw’s span.
>
> Follow .claude/pipeline/proposal-guidelines.md and write the proposal using proposal-template.md. No spike label, so read-only. Replace the issue body and apply the labels per STATE.md.

</details>
title: Link OpenClaw run traces to the openclaw_agent AI Config

body:
**Canonical LiOS.Pol phase P5/5. Required integration decision merged via [PR #15](https://github.com/limuria08-hub/Dotpol/pull/15).** No optional file-collaboration service is in scope. OpenClaw is a REQUIRED component of the complete release.

**Source of truth:** [Five-phase roadmap](https://github.com/limuria08-hub/Dotpol/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md), [machine plan](https://github.com/limuria08-hub/Dotpol/blob/main/architecture/execution-plan.yml), [agents](https://github.com/limuria08-hub/Dotpol/blob/main/AGENTS.md).

## Agent-owned tasks
- [ ] **P5.01 · A/B — Agent/plugin manifests:** one versioned registry for DataConnector, AnalysisTool, AIProvider, FieldService, ArtifactProvider and AutomationProvider; permissions/expiry/audits.
- [ ] **P5.02 · B/F — Required OpenClaw runtime:** install/pin and launch maintained OpenClaw gateway as a supported first-class LiOS.Pol component; authenticate, pair nodes, sandbox tools, enforce approval and verify local restart/reconnect. No arbitrary host shell or unreviewed skills enabled.
- [ ] **P5.03 · B/A — Channels and devices:** required authorized Telegram/WhatsApp/supported device integration through OpenClaw; inbound identity mapped to Dotpol role scope; no channel credentials copied into Dotpol client.
- [ ] **P5.04 · B/A — Do not duplicate AI:** OpenClaw transports channel messages and invokes approved Dotpol tools; PydanticAI owns political research orchestration; no second authority for projects, tools, model policy or data.
- [ ] **P5.05 · B/A — Automations:** Prefect for durable approved tasks where needed, scheduled research/monitoring, confirmation gates, retries, cost/resource caps and audit trail.
- [ ] **P5.06 · A/F — Zero-paid deployment profiles:** provide a supported local OpenClaw gateway install/launch and upgrade path as part of LiOS.Pol, plus ODK/notification service profiles where used. Compose is allowed for supported service management, not mandatory paid hosting or K3s.
- [ ] **P5.07 · F — Supply-chain compliance:** exact donor refs/versions, component/model/data licence checks, third-party notices, SBOM, update policy, permissions and security review.
- [ ] **P5.08 · E/F — Cross-device UX:** responsive desktop/tablet/mobile, keyboard, accessibility, export/import, data recovery and documented supported targets.
- [ ] **P5.09 · F — Resilience/security:** AI prompt-injection, remote-consent, unauthorized tool/cross-team access, API exposure, secrets, offline/reconnect, throughput and restore tests.
- [ ] **P5.10 · F — Exit gate:** reproducible local and approved shared deployment, final integrated research→analysis→field→report flows, release artifacts and contributor documentation.

## Acceptance gate
**Done when:** local first-run, optional organization deployment and required OpenClaw channels are independently reproducible, secure, maintained and fully documented.

## Required engineering evidence
- Code PR linked to the task ID and one canonical owner (A–F).
- Exact upstream version/license review, tests, safe local-first deployment and working end-to-end journey.
- P1 OpenClaw probe `GET /api/openclaw/status` is a preliminary read-only check; a successful mock cannot satisfy live channel/device integration. Follow the existing [P1 PR #11](https://github.com/limuria08-hub/Dotpol/pull/11).
- One OpenClaw security boundary per mutually trusted organization; restrict shell, skills, credentials and device actions.
- Never mark a work package done based only on docs, forks, screenshots, mocks or passing a gateway health probe.
title: [LiOS.Pol P5/5] OpenClaw, agents, automations, plugins and release
